A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SpeeDe3DGS work. Their complete main text, equations, figures, tables, references, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching renumbered appendix sections and tables.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments evaluating pruning and GroupFlow, including reconstruction quality, rendering speed, training time, component ablations, and qualitative results in Section 5 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds TSS hyperparameter results in Appendix A.4 and Table 11.

M1.justification: The TSP, TSS, and GroupFlow procedures, objectives, grouping rules, and inference transformations remain unchanged. The annealing period of 20,000 iterations added beside Equation 7 was already specified in v2 Section 5. Adaptive grouping appears only as future work.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same D-NeRF, HyperNeRF, NeRF-DS, Nerfies, and iPhone coverage, including the 50-scene MonoDyGauBench evaluation and standalone experiments. The new TSS ablation reuses NeRF-DS without introducing another task or scenario.

E2.justification: Tables 2–7 retain EffGS, STG-decoder, STG, RTGS, 4DGS, and DeformableGS with the same proposed variants. The newly cited motion-modeling methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Table 11 introduces controlled TSS sweeps over beta values 0.05, 0.1, and 0.2 and annealing periods 15K, 20K, and 25K. Appendix A.6 also replaces v2's conflicting RTX A4000 statement with RTX 3090 rendering and RTX A5000/A6000 training settings matching existing captions. This documents a correction, without establishing reruns.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.4 and Table 11 test sensitivity to TSS perturbation magnitude and annealing duration, including a TSP-only control. Existing component, group-count, and pruning-percentage ablations and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report three-run averages. The new TSS table follows this existing practice; it introduces no additional seed information, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 11 adds results for four nondefault TSS configurations, with PSNR ranging from 23.80 to 23.82 and SSIM from 0.8510 to 0.8517. Its TSP-only and default-TSS values reproduce v2 Table 1. Existing benchmark scores, per-scene values, and figure results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–12 retain the same mathematical content, including the sensitivity approximation and grouped SE(3) transformations. Explaining the existing mat and quat notation and discussing the J=N limiting case add exposition, without a new formal result, assumption, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same three contributions and scientific scope. The headline 6.78× pruning speedup, 13.71× combined rendering speedup, and 2.53× shorter training claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 already discusses fidelity loss under aggressive pruning and limited motion groups. New Appendix A.8 expands this with inherited baseline limitations, locally rigid motion after densification, the J=N limit, and adaptive grouping as future work. Appendix A.4 also attributes weak TSS parameter sensitivity to small interframe changes.

D1.justification: The rewritten per-scene appendix removes the unexplained ASP statement and reconciles GPU documentation with the retained timing-table captions. It clarifies the standalone codebase and metric-to-dataset mapping. v4 also attributes the existing TSS defaults to DeformableGS; those values were already disclosed in v2.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds MoSca, Gaussian-Flow, and Shape of Motion and removes RigGS. It refines the comparison by distinguishing neural inference, complex deformation computation, and reliance on 2D priors, replacing the earlier blanket characterization of costly neural inference.

P1.justification: v4 makes localized wording and grammar corrections, explains quaternion-conversion notation, and rewrites portions of related work, limitations, and per-scene documentation. It inserts two appendix subsections and updates cross-references while retaining the overall narrative and section organization.

P2.justification: v4 adds Table 11 and adjusts spacing around Tables 8–10 to accommodate it. Appendix text and Figure 5 placement reflow, and the per-scene tables are renumbered. All six figures retain their imagery, and existing table structures remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 adds useful evidence about previously untested TSS parameter sensitivity, resolves inconsistent hardware documentation, and gives a fuller account of motion-model limitations and related approaches. These improve support and clarity. The sensitivity sweep remains limited, while the method and principal empirical evidence are unchanged, making the overall improvement modest.
